title: POC Weekly Sync - Throughput Optimization
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput test results, continuous-batching tuning, concurrency targets and queueing behavior. Discussed observed tail latency spikes, KV cache hit patterns, and next steps for benchmark runs and config changes.
topics: Next benchmark runs and artifact sharing
next_steps: Redwood to share updated benchmark sheet with per-model per-config numbers (Samir) by 2026-06-12
Acuity to run 2-hour sustained load with new batching settings (Tom) by 2026-06-15
Leah to prepare recommended concurrency ramp script and example client config by 2026-06-11
Schedule follow-up check-in after sustained run (calendar invite)
action_items: Samir Patel - Share updated bench spreadsheet and raw logs - 2026-06-12
Leah Chen - Provide concurrency ramp script + recommended client settings - 2026-06-11
Tom Alvarez - Run 2-hour sustained load with new batching params and upload results - 2026-06-15
Rachel Kim - Confirm internal stakeholders for go/no-go and share acceptance SLOs - 2026-06-13
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya (Acuity): Hi, Priya here.
[00:10] Tom (Acuity): Tom here. Sorry, running a bit late, audio's on my laptop.
[00:13] Rachel (Acuity): Rachel here.
[00:15] Leah (Redwood SE): Leah on the call.
[00:18] Samir (Redwood): Cool. Agenda — quick recap of last week's changes, go over the throughput numbers from the overnight runs, then tuning suggestions and next steps. Sound good?
[00:27] Priya: Yep.
[00:29] Tom: Yep.
[00:30] [00:30] Samir (Redwood): Okay so first thing, thanks Tom for running the burst test overnight. We have the sheet, quick headline: with continuous batching enabled and batch_timeout=20ms we hit about 12.5k tokens/sec aggregate across the pod set, avg latency about 270ms, p95 around 900ms with sporadic spikes to 1.6s. Does that match what you saw?
[01:00] Tom: Yeah that's what I saw in the logs copied over. There's a csv in the drive. A few notes — the KV cash warmup seems to cause early tail spikes, also we saw queue growth around minute 12.
[01:15] Leah (Redwood SE): Quick flag — 'KV cash' is probably the transcription, it's KV cache. The warmup behavior is expected for cold keys, we should see cache hit-rate climb over the first few minutes. The queue growth suggests clients are sending more concurrent inflight requests than the runtime concurrency target.
[01:34] Priya: On the concurrency — we're currently running clients with concurrency=64 per worker container. I think that was an initial ramp.
[01:42] Leah: Right and underlying GPU concurrency target is around 20 for this model size, so the runtime does internal queuing. When the client concurrency overshoots the target you get head-of-line waits and the p95/p99 blow up.
[01:55] Rachel: Can you explain in plain english what changing batch_timeout from 20 to 10ms would do?
[02:02] Leah: Sure — smaller batch_timeout means the runtime waits less time to assemble a batch before dispatching. That lowers latency for small requests but reduces batching efficiency, so throughput drops and GPU utilization falls. It's a tradeoff.
[02:18] Tom: In last night's runs we tried batch_timeout=20,30,50ms; 50ms gave the best throughput (about 14k tokens/s) but p95 sits above 1s which for us is high.
[02:31] Samir: That's the classic latency vs cost/throughput tradeoff. For your target SLOs Priya mentioned earlier — 300ms p95 — we need to be on the lower timeout and also control client concurrency.
[02:43] Priya: Yep SLO is 300ms p95 for the primary route, secondary can be higher.
[02:48] Leah: Two levers I recommend: reduce client-side concurrency and increase the runtime target concurrency ceiling by adjusting the 'max_inflight' on the server, plus tune batch_timeout. Also enable batch-aggregation windowing to prefer short-latency requests — Redwood runtime has a hybrid policy.
[03:05] Tom: How safe is bumping max_inflight? Will it increase memory pressure?
[03:09] Leah: It can increase memory/kv usage; on GPUs with limited memory it's a trade; but for your Dedicated pool with 48GB GPUs we have headroom to increase by ~20% in our tests. We'll provide recommended settings.
[03:23] [03:23] Samir: Quick question — are you running prefix caching for the prompt shapes in the POC?
[03:28] Priya: We're using a simple prefix cache on the client but not server-side KV sharing yet.
[03:32] Leah: Enabling server-side KV (shared per-pool) would help a lot for repeated context. That reduces token compute for repeated prefixes and improves effective throughput. But it also needs warmup and eviction tuning.
[03:43] Rachel: We've got a lot of repeated system prompts so KV should help. Any gotchas?
[03:47] Leah: Mainly cold-start tail latencies and memory sizing. Also be careful with multi-tenant keys — ensure key isolation.
[03:54] Tom: Noted.
[03:55] [04:00] Samir: Ok let's look at the minute-by-minute behavior. I skimmed the logs — around minute 12 we see queue length climb to 180 requests in flight and average processing time climbs from 300ms to 1.2s.
[04:15] Priya: That's the minute when a spike of user requests came in from our test generator. We were ramping traffic to 500 rps.
[04:21] Leah: So the runtime hit sustained overload and started batching larger groups; some requests waited for earlier batches to complete (head-of-line). To mitigate we can set a soft concurrency cap at the frontend to smooth arrival, or enable token-leaky bucket on the gateway to limit bursts.
[04:36] Tom: Is that something we configure in Redwood or in our client loadgen?
[04:40] Leah: Both options — we can change the runtime config for internal queueing behavior and you can adjust loadgen concurrency. Ideally both: runtime-level backpressure + client ramp script.
[04:50] Rachel: For acceptance criteria we need consistent p95 < 300ms for a 30-minute sustained run at 350 rps.
[04:58] Samir: Great. So plan: Leah will provide a concurrency ramp script and recommended runtime params; Tom will run a 2-hour sustained run at 350 rps and upload logs; Samir will share the raw bench spreadsheet.
[05:12] Priya: Quick side — we saw a couple of errors 'context too large' in the logs, probably from a few test users. We should add a request size cap client-side.
[05:22] Leah: Good call. Also adding early rejection thresholds reduces wasted compute on oversized inputs.
[05:28] Tom: About the KV cache warmup: are there recommended pre-warm sequences?
[05:32] Leah: Yes — run a short warmup replay with the top-20 prefixes for ~10 minutes prior to test; that seeds the cache. We'll provide the list generation script.
[05:42] [06:00] Samir: Another datapoint — the model variant matters. The quantized model runs about 1.8x tokens/sec vs the fp16 baseline but sometimes gives slightly noisier outputs. Have you validated output quality?
[06:12] Rachel: We ran quick evals, quality looks acceptable for non-critical flows, but for the high-stakes summaries we want fp16.
[06:20] Leah: So we can route critical traffic to fp16 and bulk traffic to quantized variant — runtime supports route-based model variants with automatic fallback.
[06:29] Tom: That routing increases load mixing though; any performance pitfalls?
[06:33] Leah: Increased heterogeneity can lead to less efficient batching since different variants have different kernel profiles. The runtime can coalesce compatible variants but there's some overhead.
[06:41] Priya: Tradeoffs everywhere.
[06:43] Samir: Yup. Ok let's talk config specifics — Leah, what exact params do you recommend we change first?
[06:49] Leah: Incremental plan: 1) Client-side: cap concurrency per worker at 24 and introduce ramp script. 2) Server-side: set batch_timeout=15ms, increase max_inflight by 15% for this model, enable server-side KV sharing and pre-warm with top prefixes. 3) Gateway: enable soft backpressure token bucket to smooth bursts. We'll put exact values in the doc.
[07:15] Tom: If we cap client concurrency at 24 won't throughput drop drastically?
[07:19] Leah: Initially yes, but with better batching target and KV hits, effective throughput should stabilize and tail latency improve. The key is sustained runs not instantaneous bursts.
[07:30] Priya: Any monitoring tweaks we should add? Charts or metrics?
[07:34] Leah: Add queue_length, batching_rate, batch_size distribution, kv_hit_rate, gpu_utilization by model. Also token-level cost breakdown as we talked. We'll share dashboard templates.
[07:45] Samir: Also add per-route p50/p95/p99. Rachel, can you own verifying dashboards are visible to your SREs?
[07:52] Rachel: Yep I'll add them.
[07:54] [08:00] Tom: About the p99 spikes — are they mainly from cold-starts?
[08:04] Leah: Largely yes, plus occasional big requests that force long generation. Cold-starts show in the logs as high latency for first few tokens and then normalize.
[08:13] Priya: For the cold starts, would we see improvement if we keep one warm replica per zone?
[08:18] Leah: Yes, warm replicas reduce cold-starts but cost money. For Dedicated we can pin a small warm pool. We'll model the cost impact in the spreadsheet.
[08:27] Samir: I'll update the cost sheet with warm-replica scenarios.
[08:31] Rachel: On security side, small question — enabling server-side KV sharing, does that have data residency or encryption implications?
[08:38] Leah: Server-side KV uses customer data but can be configured to encrypt at rest with your KMS; access is scoped per-pool and logs audit key access. We'll include the security docs.
[08:46] Priya: Great.
[08:48] [09:00] Samir: Ok next — we saw one anomaly where batch size dropped to 1 for several seconds. Any idea why?
[09:06] Tom: That was during a client restart event where a small number of client instances were sending traffic while others were offline.
[09:12] Leah: Right, imbalance in clients can produce small batches. The runtime's continuous batching tries to collect but if arrival rate is low you'll get small batches and latency suffers. That's why smoothing at the gateway helps.
[09:25] Rachel: Could we simulate failure modes?
[09:27] Samir: We can add a chaos scenario to the next run to test resilience. Good call.
[09:33] Tom: I'll add a restart in one zone at minute 20.
[09:36] Priya: We need to capture logs around that.
[09:39] Leah: We'll add tracing hooks to correlate queue length to client events.
[09:43] [10:00] Samir: A quick note on metrics — your p95 target is 300ms but the 1.6s spikes are unacceptable. The path is client cap + batch_timeout adjustment + KV warm. Leah, you said you could push a recommended config that tends to keep p95 < 300ms at 350 rps?
[10:13] Leah: Yes based on our prior tests we are confident with the combination we just mentioned. We'll provide the exact numbers and a script to validate.
[10:21] Priya: How do we validate correctness after switching to quantized variant for bulk? We saw minor diffs in outputs.
[10:27] Leah: Use a small eval set and regression check in the same run. Redwood Optimize can run eval harnesses and surface regressions flagged by your thresholds. We'll set that up if you want.
[10:37] Rachel: Yes we want that for critical flows.
[10:39] Samir: Ok next steps recap — Leah provides scripts/docs, Samir shares updated spreadsheet+raw logs, Tom runs sustained run with ramp+chaos and uploads logs, Rachel verifies dashboards with SRE. Any additions?
[10:53] Priya: Can we get an expected timeline for when we'll see improved p95 in practice?
[10:58] Leah: If Tom runs the sustained test by 6/15 and we get logs same day, we can analyze and propose final config by 6/16-6/17. So a week-ish.
[11:09] Tom: Works for us.
[11:11] [11:30] Rachel: One more ask — can Redwood share a short doc on tradeoffs between routing to fp16 vs quantized variant, maybe a table?
[11:37] Leah: Yes, we'll include that in the deliverable pack.
[11:40] Samir: Cool. Any blockers?
[11:43] Priya: None from our side, just need the scripts.
[11:46] Tom: Nothing.
[11:48] Samir: Alright we'll follow up in the sheet. Thanks all.
[11:52] Rachel: Thanks.
[11:54] Leah: Thanks everyone.
[11:56] Samir: End.
